outcome: No proof, disproof, or scope-qualifying result on the infinitude of cousin primes has appeared since 26 January 2024; the only developments found are a December 2024 record for the largest known explicit cousin prime pair (which does not bear on infinitude per §3.1) and unrelated machine-learning work on empirical prime-density prediction.
summary: The infinitude of cousin primes (Polignac's conjecture for gap 4) remains an open problem with no resolution, partial resolution, or bound movement since 26 January 2024. The two pre-snapshot claimed proofs the triage pass found — Du's 2005 arXiv preprint (math/0510329, category math.GM, last revised 2005-10-24, never published in a peer-reviewed venue) and the 2019 arXiv preprint by [author of 1903.05410] claiming a proof of both the Twin Prime and Polignac/cousin-prime conjectures (category math.GM, revised 15 times through 2022-06-02) — remain unaccepted preprints with no subsequent endorsement, and neither has been withdrawn or formally reviewed; they predate the window regardless. The current Wikipedia 'Cousin prime' article (checked live, 2026-09) still states infinitude is unproven and conditional only on the (also unproven) first Hardy–Littlewood conjecture, and lists no claimed proof as accepted. The one dated, verifiable event inside the window is the December 2024 update to the largest-known explicit cousin prime pair (S. Batalov, 86,138 digits, surpassing an earlier 51,934-digit record), reported on the Cousin prime Wikipedia article and prime-records sites. Under §3.1, a record extension narrows where an answer could hide but does not answer the existence question itself, so it is excluded as a status-changing event ('An existence or infinitude question moves only when it is answered ... A record counts only where the record is the question') — this bullet is not a 'largest known object' bullet, it is an infinitude bullet. I also found unrelated 2025-2026 work applying deep learning to prime classification: 'PrimeFamilyNet' (arXiv 2604.02383, Manik Kakkar) trains a residual network to recognize twin/cousin/sexy/Chen/etc. primes and reports that a version trained only to 10^9 'reproduced the correct asymptotic direction without density supervision, corroborating Hardy-Littlewood k-tuple predictions.' This is empirical/statistical corroboration of a density heuristic via a classifier, not a proof, a case settled, or a bound on the conjecture; it does not change what a careful person would write in this bullet's entry, so it is not counted as progress. I also encountered an unverifiable web-search summary claiming 'a 2026 preprint reformulated the cousin prime problem within a deterministic framework and showed that infinitely many cousin prime pairs exist' — I could not find this preprint under any independent search or by fetching candidate arXiv IDs, and the only paper resolvable at the cited ID (2604.02383) was the unrelated PrimeFamilyNet classifier paper. I treat this claim as unsubstantiated and it is not the basis for any finding in this record.
competing_reading: None of the candidate events (the two stale unaccepted preprints, the December 2024 record pair, or the PrimeFamilyNet paper) plausibly supports a status other than 'open'. The closest case for a different reading would be treating the December 2024 largest-known-pair record as 'progress', but the rules explicitly exclude record extensions on infinitude questions from counting, so I did not classify it that way.
what_would_settle_it: A peer-reviewed or expert-digested proof (or disproof) of Polignac's conjecture for gap 4, or an accepted preprint specifically addressing the cousin-prime case (as opposed to a general, unaccepted claim about twin primes bundled with a cousin-prime corollary).
